title: Shipping delay and repeat purchase
demonstrates: A joined cohort comparison, a two-proportion z-test, and a causal interpretation that the verifier rejects.
question: Do shipping delays appear to affect repeat purchasing?

report.question: Do shipping delays appear to affect repeat purchasing?
report.executive_summary: repeat_purchase_rate rose from 71.06 in 2023-12-01 to 82.44 in 2024-01-01 (11.38). late_delivery_rate rose from 8.94 in 2024-10-01 to 14.26 in 2024-11-01 (5.32). Across acquisition_channel, social has the highest repeat_purchase_rate at 69.81 and affiliate the lowest at 65.58.
key_findings: repeat_purchase_rate rose from 71.06 in 2023-12-01 to 82.44 in 2024-01-01 (11.38).
late_delivery_rate rose from 8.94 in 2024-10-01 to 14.26 in 2024-11-01 (5.32).
Across acquisition_channel, social has the highest repeat_purchase_rate at 69.81 and affiliate the lowest at 65.58.
Across region, Southwest has the highest repeat_purchase_rate at 69.35 and Northeast the lowest at 66.91.

Measured rate: late = 0.50, on_time = 0.70. A two-proportion z-test on late=3,401, on_time=26,599 returned p = 2.15e-122 with Cohen's h = -0.412; the difference is statistically significant at the 5% level.

res_0af512dd90ab.sql:
WITH base AS (
SELECT date_trunc('month', signup_date) AS period, 100.0 * SUM(is_repeat) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS "repeat_purchase_rate"
FROM (
WITH first_ship AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id,
         s.is_late      AS first_delivery_late,
         s.carrier      AS first_carrier,
         s.delivery_days AS first_delivery_days
  FROM orders o
  JOIN shipping_events s ON s.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.is_first_order
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.signup_date,
  c.customer_segment,
  c.region,
  c.acquisition_channel,
  COALESCE(oc.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(oc.order_count, 0) > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_repeat,
  f.first_delivery_late,
  f.first_carrier,
  f.first_delivery_days,
  CASE WHEN f.first_delivery_late THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END AS first_delivery_status
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN order_counts oc ON oc.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN first_ship f   ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
) AS m
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', signup_date)
ORDER BY date_trunc('month', signup_date)
)
SELECT period, "repeat_purchase_rate",
  LAG("repeat_purchase_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period) AS prev_period,
  ROUND("repeat_purchase_rate" - LAG("repeat_purchase_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period), 6) AS change_abs,
  ROUND(100.0 * ("repeat_purchase_rate" - LAG("repeat_purchase_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period))
        / NULLIF(ABS(LAG("repeat_purchase_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period)), 0), 4) AS change_pct
FROM base
ORDER BY period

res_4a21d22ef620.sql:
WITH base AS (
SELECT date_trunc('month', shipped_date) AS period, 100.0 * SUM(is_late_int) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS "late_delivery_rate"
FROM (
SELECT
  s.order_id,
  s.carrier,
  s.region,
  s.shipped_date,
  s.delivered_date,
  s.delivery_days,
  s.promised_days,
  CASE WHEN s.is_late THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_late_int,
  c.customer_segment,
  c.acquisition_channel
FROM shipping_events s
JOIN orders o    ON o.order_id = s.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
) AS m
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', shipped_date)
ORDER BY date_trunc('month', shipped_date)
)
SELECT period, "late_delivery_rate",
  LAG("late_delivery_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period) AS prev_period,
  ROUND("late_delivery_rate" - LAG("late_delivery_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period), 6) AS change_abs,
  ROUND(100.0 * ("late_delivery_rate" - LAG("late_delivery_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period))
        / NULLIF(ABS(LAG("late_delivery_rate") OVER (ORDER BY period)), 0), 4) AS change_pct
FROM base
ORDER BY period

WITH base AS (
SELECT "region" AS "region", 100.0 * SUM(is_repeat) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS "repeat_purchase_rate"
FROM (
WITH first_ship AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id,
         s.is_late      AS first_delivery_late,
         s.carrier      AS first_carrier,
         s.delivery_days AS first_delivery_days
  FROM orders o
  JOIN shipping_events s ON s.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.is_first_order
),
order_counts AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.signup_date,
  c.customer_segment,
  c.region,
  c.acquisition_channel,
  COALESCE(oc.order_count, 0) AS order_count,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(oc.order_count, 0) > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_repeat,
  f.first_delivery_late,
  f.first_carrier,
  f.first_delivery_days,
  CASE WHEN f.first_delivery_late THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END AS first_delivery_status
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN order_counts oc ON oc.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN first_ship f   ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
) AS m
GROUP BY "region"
ORDER BY "region"
)
SELECT "region", "repeat_purchase_rate",
  CASE WHEN MIN("repeat_purchase_rate") OVER () >= 0 THEN
    ROUND(100.0 * "repeat_purchase_rate" / NULLIF(SUM("repeat_purchase_rate") OVER (), 0), 4)
  END AS share_of_total_pct,
  ROUND("repeat_purchase_rate" - MAX("repeat_purchase_rate") OVER (), 6) AS diff_vs_best,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "repeat_purchase_rate" DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_desc
FROM base
ORDER BY "repeat_purchase_rate" DESC NULLS LAST
